## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no results yet, so no deviation is ruled out. Two points come from reasoning, not data. First, the obs channel order cannot matter for these nets, because every trunk starts with a 1x1 conv over all channels, and that conv can learn any channel order. Second, an obs transposed or flipped relative to the mask is the same problem as the mask and action layout being transposed or flipped relative to the obs, and the reference's layout hedge already covers that case. So round 1 runs: the reference unchanged; a 16-layout hedge (8 grid symmetries times type-major and type-minor order); a 5x5 head; a hedge on the DONE index (last or first); an extra path that does not assume any layout; and a version with all hedges combined. Every file reads the number of maps per layout from the mask itself (n_place / (Y*X)), so a per-layer or different type count still lines up. If n_place doesn't divide evenly, it embeds the mask and the logits with Linear layers instead. Any nonzero training success will be the signal to follow.

### Round 2
Round 1 was all 0, including training success. The parameter counts give facts about this world. r1c1 has 53,130 parameters, which fits exactly with in_channels 27 (Z=6) and k=4 types on 64 cells, so n_place is 256. r1c5's count gives n_actions = 257. Round 1 therefore rules out: a non-grid action count; the 16 symmetry and type-major/minor layouts; and footprint or anchor offsets within 5x5. Permuted obs channels are also ruled out, because a 1x1 stem gives the same result under any channel order. One finding matters a lot: the DONE-at-index-0 hedge was never active. Its offset test needed o+n_place < n_actions, which drops offset 1 when n_actions = n_place+1. r1c4 has the same parameter count as r1c1, which confirms it. Still untested: DONE at index 0; obs stored in channel-last or other memory orders; action orders with the type in the middle (YTX, XTY); obs shifted or scrambled relative to the actions; and reward deviations such as a sparse terminal reward.

### Round 3
After 12 trials, every dev score is 0. These results rule out the following as the only deviation: the 4 or 16 mask/output layouts, all 6 axis orders, DONE at index 0, footprints that a 5x5 window can cover, obs memory order (yxc, xyc, ycx), channel permutations (the 1x1 stem is unaffected by them), and a sparse reward combined with these hedges. The only nonzero training success was r2c6, the dense obs cell-remap (0.0005, about one exact build). That is weak and may be noise, but under the program it is the only signal, so 4 of the 6 candidates build on the remap with one change each. The other bets are: a misalignment that differs per channel (for example the target flipped relative to the build), an unknown permutation between obs cells and action cells, and non-local dynamics. Only one round remains after this one, so if all six score 0 again, round 4 should test radical deviations and not refine.

### Round 4
All 18 trials scored 0 on dev, and training success was at most 0.0005. Parameter counts confirm the spec is as described: k=4, Y*X=64, in_channels=27 and n_actions=257. That rules out a grid-size or action-count mismatch and a moved DONE index.

The trunk's 1x1 stem would learn a permuted channel order, and that hedge also scored 0. Every hedge on the action layout or on obs-to-action alignment also scored 0: 16 symmetries, 6 axis orders, flips, learned remaps, a dense flat head and a 5x5 head. So did one long-horizon recipe and 400k-step training.

The remaining suspects are not about layout:
- obs or reward on an unexpected scale, or value gradients swamping the shared trunk;
- the policy collapsing onto DONE or into early determinism;
- sparse or delayed reward;
- dynamics that are not local.

This last round keeps the summed 4-layout hedge and the remap, and changes three things: a normalised stem, a separate critic, and either attention or exploration and horizon settings.
